Specialist: route-and-logistics

You are the route and logistics specialist on a trip-planning tool.
You propose the legs this trip is made of — drives, rides, transfers, ferries and trains — with the stops that make a long one bearable.

You propose options. You never write a schedule: nothing you return says which day it falls on, what order things happen in, or what time anything starts. Another part of this tool packs the days, in code.

Rules, and they are not negotiable:
- Reply with JSON and nothing else, in exactly this shape:
{
  "candidates": [
    {
      "title": "short, and never an itinerary",
      "summary": "why this is worth doing, in a sentence or two",
      "location": { "kind": "at", "place": { "name": "...", "locality": "... or null", "coordinates": null } },
      "durationMinutes": 0,
      "cost": { "currency": "ISO-4217", "low": 0, "high": 0, "basis": "per-person | per-party", "provenance": { "kind": "model-asserted" } },
      "season": { "from": "MM-DD", "to": "MM-DD" },
      "bookingLeadTimeDays": 0
    }
  ]
}
- At most 6 candidates. Fewer is a fine answer; an empty list is a fine answer.
- Anything you do not know is null. A duration nobody measured is null, not a plausible ninety minutes. A season nobody checked is null — which is not the same as all year, and all year is written {"from":"01-01","to":"12-31"}.
- Costs are bands with a currency and a basis, never a single figure and never a quote. Do not total anything.
- A slot that says "not answered" is unknown to you. Say in the summary what you could not account for, and propose anyway. Never invent the answer and never refuse to propose.
- Never book anything, never ask for payment details, and never present what you write as clearance to go anywhere.
- Every candidate is a movement, so its location is {"kind":"between","from":{...},"to":{...}} with **both** ends as places. Endpoints in the title are not endpoints, and a candidate that puts them there is discarded.
- This trip has 13 days.
- **Nothing you propose may be longer than 300 minutes.** That is the party's own answer about how much a day holds, translated into minutes. Something longer has to be split into parts that each fit, or not proposed — a candidate over that ceiling is discarded and the plan comes back missing this part of itself.

messages.content:
Here is the trip. It is everything you get.

Shape: multi-city
Leaving from: Halifax
Going to: Central Europe
Dates: 12 nights somewhere between 2027-05-01 and 2027-06-15
Travellers: 2
Ages that change the plan: not answered
Access needs: not answered
Budget: comfortable, as a feeling rather than a figure
Appetite for effort: moderate
Roughest night they will accept: hotel
Would rule the trip out: No internal flights

About this multi-city:
Cities: Vienna, Ljubljana, Trieste
Transport between them: train
Fewest nights in any one: 3
In their words: The order is not fixed — we picked those three because the trains between them looked reasonable, and we would drop one rather than rush all three.

candidates.title: Railjet over the Semmering line to Graz
candidates.summary: First half of the Vienna–Ljubljana rail link. The direct train runs about six hours, which is over the party's daily ceiling, so it is split at Graz, a city worth a stopover. Access needs were not answered, so step-free boarding and luggage help are not accounted for.

candidates.title: Cross-border train via Maribor to the Slovenian capital
candidates.summary: Second half of the Vienna–Ljubljana link, through Styrian wine country and the Drava valley. It may involve a change at Maribor depending on the timetable, which was not checked for May–June 2027.

candidates.title: Karst rail line down to the Adriatic
candidates.summary: Rail between Ljubljana and Trieste is sparse and usually needs a change, at Sežana or Villa Opicina. It is still well short of a full day. Whether a direct service runs in 2027 is unchecked; a coach is the faster fallback if the trains do not suit.

candidates.title: Fast train south via the Koralm line into Carinthia
candidates.summary: First half of a Vienna–Trieste route that skips Ljubljana, for use if the party drops it. The new Koralm tunnel should speed this leg up, but its timings were not verified.

candidates.title: Cross-border regional train over the Alps to the coast
candidates.summary: Second half of the Vienna–Trieste option, by the cross-border regional train via Udine through the Canal valley. Its frequency and luggage space in 2027 are unknown.

candidatesAccepted.title: Central hotel in Vienna's inner districts
candidatesAccepted.summary: A comfortable mid-to-upper-range hotel near the Ringstrasse or in Neubau/Wieden keeps sights walkable and the Hauptbahnhof a short tram ride away for onward trains. Ages and access needs were not answered, so check lift access and room layout before choosing.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel near Vienna Hauptbahnhof
candidatesAccepted.summary: A practical comfortable hotel beside the main station suits a train-based trip and makes departure days easy. Access needs were not answered, so step-free routes are unverified.

candidatesAccepted.title: Old-town hotel in Ljubljana
candidatesAccepted.summary: Ljubljana's compact, largely pedestrian centre rewards staying by the river; a comfortable boutique hotel there fits a moderate pace. Inventory is small, so book well ahead in late spring. Access needs were not answered; old buildings may lack lifts.

candidatesAccepted.title: Seafront or Borgo Teresiano hotel in Trieste
candidatesAccepted.summary: A comfortable hotel near Piazza Unità or the Borgo Teresiano puts the waterfront and cafés on the doorstep and Trieste Centrale within walking distance. Ages and access needs were not answered; Trieste is hilly away from the waterfront.

candidatesAccepted.title: Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna
candidatesAccepted.summary: One of Europe's great picture galleries (Bruegel, Vermeer, Habsburg collections) — a calm, moderate-effort half day. Access needs were not answered, so step-free access has not been checked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Schönbrunn Palace and gardens
candidatesAccepted.summary: The Habsburg summer palace with state rooms and extensive gardens, at their best in May–June. Timed palace tickets may sell out. Access needs were not answered, and the gardens involve a fair amount of walking.

candidatesAccepted.title: Evening at the Vienna State Opera
candidatesAccepted.summary: A performance at the Staatsoper suits a comfortable budget. The season usually runs into late June, but this has not been checked for 2027. Ages and access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Ljubljana old town and castle
candidatesAccepted.summary: A compact, walkable old town along the Ljubljanica river, with a funicular up to the castle. The effort is moderate. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Lake Bled outing from Ljubljana
candidatesAccepted.summary: Visit the lake, a pletna boat out to the island church, and a gentle shoreline walk. This is the time at the lake only; travel from Ljubljana is not included. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Postojna Cave
candidatesAccepted.summary: A large show cave with an underground train and a guided walk, and an easy stop between Ljubljana and Trieste. The cave is cool inside. Access needs were not answered, and the walk has some slopes.

candidatesAccepted.title: Miramare Castle and park, Trieste
candidatesAccepted.summary: A 19th-century seaside castle with landscaped grounds on the Gulf of Trieste, which make for a relaxed half day. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Trieste historic cafés and Piazza Unità
candidatesAccepted.summary: Trieste's literary coffeehouse culture around Europe's largest sea-facing square: low effort and very characteristic of the city. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Heuriger evening in Vienna's wine villages
candidatesAccepted.summary: A meal at a traditional Heuriger wine tavern on Vienna's edge, with young local wine and a cold buffet among the vineyards — a Viennese ritual rather than just dinner. Dietary restrictions, ages and access needs were not answered, so check the buffet and hillside terrain suit the party.

candidatesAccepted.title: Classic Viennese coffee house sitting
candidatesAccepted.summary: An unhurried coffee and cake (Sachertorte, apple strudel) in a historic Viennese café, where lingering is the point. Dietary needs were not answered; pastries are wheat- and dairy-heavy.

place.name: Historic coffee houses (e.g. Café Sperl, Café Central)

candidatesAccepted.title: Naschmarkt grazing in Vienna
candidatesAccepted.summary: Wander and snack through Vienna's best-known market stalls and small eateries, picking what suits you. A flexible option given dietary restrictions were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Ljubljana Open Kitchen street-food market
candidatesAccepted.summary: A weekly outdoor food market where Slovenian chefs cook regional dishes by the river — a lively way to taste the country in one place. Its operating season and weekday were not verified, and dietary needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Slovenian tasting menu dinner in Ljubljana
candidatesAccepted.summary: A comfortable-budget sit-down dinner showcasing modern Slovenian cooking and local wines. Dietary restrictions were not answered — mention any when reserving.

place.name: Modern Slovenian restaurant in the old town

candidatesAccepted.title: Trieste buffet and café tradition
candidatesAccepted.summary: Lunch at a traditional Triestine 'buffet' serving boiled pork and Central European-Italian fare, followed by coffee ordered the local way in a historic café. Pork-heavy menus; dietary needs were not answered.

place.name: Traditional buffets and historic cafés (e.g. Buffet da Pepi, Caffè San Marco)

candidatesAccepted.title: ETIAS travel authorisation check
candidatesAccepted.summary: If both travellers hold visa-exempt passports such as Canadian ones, the EU's ETIAS pre-travel authorisation is expected to apply to Schengen entry by 2027, covering Austria, Slovenia and Italy. Nationality was not given, so confirm which entry rules apply on the official EU site. Fee and processing times are my understanding, not checked, and nothing here is clearance to travel.

candidatesAccepted.title: Vienna–Ljubljana–Trieste rail tickets
candidatesAccepted.summary: The plan depends on the trains. Vienna–Ljubljana has direct daytime services, and discounted ÖBB fares tend to sell out. Direct Ljubljana–Trieste trains have been limited or seasonal, so check the May–June timetable, or a bus fallback, before deciding whether to drop a city. The order is open, so price both directions.

candidatesAccepted.title: Travel medical and cancellation insurance
candidatesAccepted.summary: Out-of-country medical cover is worth arranging for two people across three countries. Ages and access needs were not answered, and both can change premiums and eligibility a lot, so treat this band loosely. Check whether existing credit card or employer cover already applies.

candidatesAccepted.title: EU-wide eSIM data plan
candidatesAccepted.summary: One EU data eSIM works across Austria, Slovenia and Italy under EU roaming rules, which keeps train apps and maps working without per-country SIMs. It is usually cheaper than Canadian carrier roaming packs. Check that both phones are unlocked and eSIM-capable.

gaps.detail: This part of the plan was left out to keep the run inside its budget. Re-planning with a larger budget would fill it in.
Nothing was checked about conditions or kit: this trip does not turn on them.
